title: The reconcile suite takes 10-15 minutes and nothing runs in parallel
description:
`internal/reconcile` takes 10-15 minutes under `-short` and is the whole cost of
the gate. Measured across this session's runs: 604s, 614s, 725s, 727s, 888s,
1063s. A wave-2 worker running `make test-short` sat for 736s on one invocation.

Every worker pays it, several times, and so does every gate. On a four-worker
wave that is roughly an hour of wall clock and real provider spend on agents
doing nothing but waiting.

## What it is NOT

Not sleeps. The longest wait in the package is 2s; everything else is 20-50ms.
Nothing is polling badly.

## What it IS

Process spawning, multiplied. 80 tests, 67 of which build a full fixture. Each
fixture creates a real git repo plus a bare origin (7 git invocations before a
test starts), and each test then drives whole reconciler runs that fork git for
every single operation and launch real worker processes through the built
executor binary. One representative test (TestAMergeRefusalIsHeldForAPerson...)
takes 6.2s ON ITS OWN.

## The obvious lever: nothing runs in parallel

`grep -c 't.Parallel()' internal/reconcile/*_test.go` is ZERO across all 16 test
files. The isolation needed for it already exists:

- Every fixture gets its own `t.TempDir()` root, its own repo, its own bare
  origin, and its own `StateRoot` (harness_test.go:414).
- The one piece of shared state, `executorBin`, is built once in `TestMain` and
  only read afterwards (harness_test.go:32-46).
- Teardown is already fixture-scoped: `stopEverything` kills only the pids from
  `f.handles` (harness_test.go:600-637), never a broad `pkill`. There is no
  `pkill`/`killall` anywhere in the package's tests.

So the isolation is there; the annotation is missing.

## Do

1. Establish the real ceiling first: run the package with `-parallel N` for a few
   N on this machine and record wall-clock. Each test forks git AND worker
   processes, so the limit is host load, not correctness — find where returns
   stop and set the default there rather than guessing.
2. Add `t.Parallel()` where it is safe. Prove safety rather than assume it: any
   test that asserts on host-wide state, on process-group behaviour across
   attempts, or on the executor state root outside its own fixture, stays
   serial and says why in a comment.
3. Anything left serial gets a one-line reason. A test that cannot be parallel
   is a fact about the design worth writing down.
4. Consider a cheaper fixture for the tests that do not need a full origin —
   but only after measuring, and only if it does not weaken what they assert.
   Fixture realism is why these tests catch what they catch; do not trade it
   for speed.

## Do not

Do not reach for `-short` skips to hit a number. The suite's value is that it
drives the real reconciler against real git with real worker processes, and
this epic has already been burned twice by tests that passed for the wrong
reason. Faster, not thinner.

acceptance_criteria: make test-short completes materially faster than the ~600-900s baseline for internal/reconcile, with the achieved wall-clock recorded against the measured baseline; the chosen -parallel value is justified by measurement on this machine rather than guessed; every test left serial carries a one-line reason; no test is weakened, skipped or moved behind a build tag to reach the number, and the suite still drives the real reconciler against real git and real worker processes; the full suite is green on three consecutive runs to prove no flakiness was introduced by parallelism.
